cell.n: 110 problems: shard 0/3 of hard328 (indices 0, 3, 6, ..., 327), spread evenly over the easier and harder halves
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0; seed 95000000, sample s of problem i uses seed + 10000*s + i (run_cell rule)
cell.grader: v3; plurality vote over the 12 extracted answers grouped with rln4_lib.agree, capped samples abstain, ties to the lowest sample index

cells.command: uv run tools/gpu.py submit l40s --hours 2 -- "bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model base --prompt cue --set hard328 --shard 0/3 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --max-tokens 2048 --samples 12 --restarts 0 --seed 95000000 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
cells.readout: Right answers (grader v3) of the plurality vote over 12 samples on the 110 problems, computed from answers.jsonl; a sample that hits the 2,048 cap gives no answer
cells.why: f2-m01 says hard328 solutions take 6,000-14,000 tokens, so 2,048-token samples reach only the short-solution problems: roughly RL-length quartile Q1 plus a few from Q2, about 85 of 328 (the base is right within 4k on 81 of 328 per sample, result-1b6bf2; the 12-sample vote at 4k reached 139, result-6e7b64). So the vote stays near 28 of 110 however many samples are added. training-m04 fixes each problem's distribution over final values in pretraining, regardless of answer length, so the cap only censors samples: the finished short samples converge on the same mode as the full-length vote (192 of 328 over 4 samples, about 66 of 110), losing only the problems where no sample finishes, which gives about 50.

best_base.note: Best base-only count with 12 samples on hard328: the Karpathy-loop method (plain prompt, T 0.6, 12 samples capped at 4,096, vote) got 139 of 328. Scaled to the 110 shard problems: 139 x 110/328 = 46.6. No base-only cell has a count on exactly these 110 problems.

cell.prompt: base pair1 prompt with the cue prefilled as opening text (' line!\n\nOkay', frozen4.json prefill_text), as in the Think-SFT cue cells
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0, repetition penalty 1.0; seed 47000000 + index
cell.cap: 32,768 generated tokens (each answer also read as if cut at 16,384)

cells.command: uv run tools/gpu.py submit l40s --hours 2 -- "bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.theory.jobs.free_cell --model think_sft --opening-text $' line!\n\nOkay' --set math500 --shard 0/2 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --max-tokens 32768 --samples 1 --seed 47000000 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
cells.readout: Among the answers that pass 16,384 generated tokens and then finish before 32,768 (finish reason stop), the share that grader v3 scores right. This equals the 32k-minus-16k gain divided by the number of such answers. About 12 are expected (Think-SFT cue has about 24 cap hits per 500 on MATH-500, result-bf6124).
cells.unit: fraction of answers (right / finished past 16,384 tokens)
cells.why: f2-m04 says an answer that used to abstain at the cap and now finishes becomes a mostly wrong guess. The only board measurement of such conversions for Think-SFT is 23 right of 93 on hard328 (result-c8b994). So the share right stays under half even on MATH-500, centre near 0.25-0.3. sampling-m05 says cut samples finish right at the rate of the model's long finished answers, which it calls high for Think-SFT (68.2% of its finished answers over 12,000 tokens are right on hard328, result-b006f5, and MATH-500 is easier), which gives about 0.68.
